title: COSMONAUTS CONDUCT RUSSIAN SPACEWALK OUTSIDE SPACE STATION
description: Outside the International Space Station, Expedition 66 Commander Anton Shkaplerov and Flight Engineer Pyotr Dubrov of Roscosmos conducted a spacewalk on Jan. 19 to outfit the Prichal node module for the future arrival of Russian visiting vehicles. Prichal launched in November from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan. It was the 246th spacewalk in support of space station assembly, maintenance and upgrades, the third in Shkaplerov’s career and the fourth for Dubrov. transcript.text: Russian spacewalk 51 will be conducted by Anton Shkaplerov.
EV1 in the red stripes and Pyotr Dubrov,
EV2 in the blue stripes.
After egressing from Poisk
with the EVA bundle, EV1 will translate to the Strella operators
post where he'll maneuver EV2 to the Nauka module,
also known as MLM.
EV1 will egress the operators post
and translate the EVA bundle nadir to EV2.
Both crew will translate along the Nauka handrails to the newly installed Russian
node module, where they'll be performing most of their work for the spacewalk.
When they arrive at the node module the crew will split the EVA bundle
and work to install the first shortcut handrail.
After, EV2 will translate to connector patch panel 26, EV1 will place
the Kurs P cables and cable clamps and hand the connectors to EV2 for mating.
After handing
off the Kurs P cables, Anton will meet patch panel to connectors
one two and three to the unused connector panel.
They'll then mate patch
panel one kours P cables.
Anton will then move on to install
ARVKA and Pyotr will install AOVKA.
These are two antennas located on the nadir side of the node module.
EV1 will then translate to the Nauka node interface
where he'll mate and route the TV cable between the two modules.
Meanwhile, Pyotr
will remove the TV camera from its current port.
Anton then translates to the nadir side of the node,
wher he'll install the docking, monitoring, target and docking
target for future visiting vehicles.
Pyotr will complete the reinstallation
of the TV camera at its new location.
EV1 starts the first round of jettisons
with two empty containers in the AOVKA antenna cover.
Meanwhile, Russian ground personnel will perform a Kurs
hardware test and a TV camera connectivity check out.
After Anton is complete with the jettison,
he'll proceed to remove a floodlight from the node module.
Pyotr will continue installing additional load limiters,
which help with spacewalk hook operations.
Both will meet back up to install
another shortcut handrail.
They'll then work together to remove three antennas
that are no longer needed. These antennas will be
strategically tossed overboard in the station aft direction.
This will be the second and final round of jettisons.
The crew will then perform inventories of their tools
and begin translating back up Nauka and
Strella.
They'll arrive back at the air lock on the Poisk module.
This is where they'll stow the remaining hardware,
finishing Russian spacewalk 51 with crew ingress and hatch closure.
